card.statement:
The group scheme $\widetilde{G}_{\mathbf{Z}}$ is the unique reductive group over $\mathbf{Z}$ which admits a split torus and whose root datum is dual to that of $G$.

In fact, below we will prove a slightly more precise result: we will construct a maximal torus of $\widetilde{G}_{\mathbf{Z}}$ whose group of characters identifies with $X_{*}(T)$, and show that the root datum of $\widetilde{G}_{\mathbf{Z}}$ with respect to this maximal torus is dual to the root datum of $(G,T)$. For a general $\mathbf{k}$, since $\widetilde{G}_{\mathbf{k}}\cong\mathrm{Spec}(\mathbf{k})\times_{\mathrm{Spec}(\mathbf{Z})}\widetilde{G}_{\mathbf{Z}}$ (see (13.1)), Theorem 14.1 determines $\widetilde{G}_{\mathbf{k}}$ also up to isomorphism.

When $\mathbf{k}$ is a field of characteristic $0$, this description3030 30

Note that in this setting there are two different groups that we have denoted $\widetilde{G}_{\mathbf{k}}$: the one constructed in Section 9 using Tannakian reconstruction, and the one constructed “by hand” in Section 13. These two groups are canonically identified thanks to [Mi, Theorem X.1.2]. has already been proved in Theorem 9.8; this special case will play an important role in the proof below. In fact, a result of Prasad–Yu [PY, Proposition 1.5] ensures that a flat affine group scheme $H$ over $\mathbf{Z}$ such that $\mathrm{Spec}(\mathbf{k})\times_{\mathrm{Spec}(\mathbf{Z})}H$ is a connected reductive group for any algebraically closed3131 31

As stated in [PY], the claim requires this property rather when $\mathbf{k}$ is either $\mathbf{Q}$ or a finite field $\mathbf{F}_{p}$. But an affine group scheme over a field is reductive iff its base change to an algebraic closure of the field is reductive; this follows from the fact that smoothness can be checked on this base change, see [GW, Remark 6.30(2)], and similarly for connectedness, see Footnote 3. field $\mathbf{k}$, whose dimension is independent of $\mathbf{k}$, is necessarily reductive. Hence what remains to be done is:

construct a subgroup scheme of $\widetilde{G}_{\mathbf{Z}}$ which is a split torus;

check that for an algebraic closure $\mathbf{k}$ of a finite field, the group scheme $\widetilde{G}_{\mathbf{k}}$ is reductive;

show that the base change to $\mathbf{k}$ of our $\mathbf{Z}$ -torus is a maximal torus of $\widetilde{G}_{\mathbf{k}}$;

and finally, show that $\widetilde{G}_{\mathbf{k}}$ has the appropriate root datum with respect to this maximal torus.

Here (1) will be easy, and based on the same arguments as for fields of characteristic $0$, see §14.2. The proof of (2)–(4) will rely on another result of Prasad–Yu [PY, Theorem 1.2] which, in our setting, characterizes reductive group schemes over $\mathbf{Z}_{p}$ in terms of properties of their base change to $\mathbf{Q}_{p}$ and to an algebraic closure of $\mathbf{F}_{p}$. (More precisely, this result will be needed to show that $\widetilde{G}_{\mathbf{k}}$ is reduced; the other properties will be checked directly.)

14.2 First properties

For any $\mathbf{k}$, by construction $\widetilde{G}_{\mathbf{k}}$ is an affine group scheme over $\mathbf{k}$. Moreover, this group scheme is flat over $\mathbf{k}$ by Proposition 13.2.

paper.title: Notes on the geometric Satake equivalence
paper.abstract: These notes are devoted to a detailed exposition of the proof of the Geometric Satake Equivalence for general coefficients, following Mirkovic-Vilonen.
